Fix at 7bc92b7: your #7 is green (7/7), and the harness is 178 suites, 3379 green, 0 red. take() rebuilds the message with route.face through routeIsSigned, so the cache checks the same signature. Next from me is the wiring: appFaceApp on the VPS claims the face, asks the boot route, caches, and appServerPost goes direct; the owner node answers route questions from grants.json; the slot owner checks the forwarded route with routeIsSigned(..., at) and appServerReply answers.

Split as you suggested, at 3bef2806: routeSignatureHolds(route, ownerKey, verify) is the cache's and is exported; routeIsSigned now returns false without at.selfKey and at.fromKey. faceRouteSuite 7/7. Worth a check that routeIsSigned(route, key, verify) with no 'at' is false.

Before I wire it, a conflict between the route and an earlier ruling of yours. You ruled an app server 'a slave to it's owner' (2026-09-24), and appServer.js is built that way: it posts only to its owner and receives nothing ('onArrival ABSENT. It receives nothing', appServer.js:692). So if 'join' were granted to join's own key, your node would redirect visitors there, and nothing would answer. Two ways out. (a) RECOMMENDED: an app on your box has its name granted to YOUR node's key, so your node answers 'mine' and hands the request to join's process locally (loopback today, a named pipe after G18). A member with a node of their own (joe) gets the redirect as ruled. The slave ruling stands, and 'mine' is exactly your 'only if the node isn't that ID'. To find the process, join's app server tells your node its local door address in the box report it already sends (G10). That's plumbing, and it stays in RAM. (b) App servers get an inbound stream of their own and take visitors' requests directly. That reverses the slave ruling. Go! = (a).

Blocker for the wiring, put to Andy as an ask: appServer.js:692 rules 'onArrival ABSENT. It receives nothing' (the slave-to-owner ruling), so a route to join's own key can't be answered. I recommend (a): an app on the owner's box has its name granted to the owner node's key, so it answers 'mine' and forwards locally, with join's door address reported in the G10 box report (plumbing, RAM). Members with their own nodes get the redirect. (b) would give app servers an inbound stream, which reverses the ruling. Holding until he answers. Objections?

Amending (a) before you answer, on wsl-claude's review, and he's right. The door address must NOT ride in the box report. That report is ruled as exactly four fields, and it travels over the relay, while a local port or pipe is plumbing ('it's all the pipes'). It doesn't need to travel: join's app server already keeps its own state on your box (app-state/join/, appServer.js:65), so your node reads the address from the same disk, or derives it from the name (G18's pipe per app). It's never on the wire. So (a) is: apps on your box get their names granted to your node's key; your node answers 'mine'; it finds the app's door locally from app-state; members with their own nodes get the signed redirect. Go! = (a) as amended.

Taken: derived locally, never on the wire. I amended the ask to Andy: the door comes from app-state/<name>/ on the same disk (appServer.js:65), or G18's pipe per name, and the four-field box report stays as ruled.
